battle.name: 太原之戰
battle.brief: 天寶十四載末，安祿山親率叛軍西進，兵鋒直指河東重鎮太原。李光弼以弩機分層列於城頭與女牆，交叉覆蓋城根，白日攀城之敵盡被壓在牆外；叛軍穴地、架雲梯、推撞車，屢攻不下，至德二載史思明傾力圍城，亦終因糧道不繼而解圍，太原自此不失。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 太原之戰是安史之亂中唐廷與安史叛軍在河東重鎮太原一帶的反覆爭奪，交戰一方是安祿山及其子安慶緒、將領史思明與崔乾祐所率領的叛軍集團，另一方是唐廷的河東、朔方兩軍，以及在亂局中歸附唐室的蕃部騎兵。唐方以河東節度使郭子儀總攬河東軍政，其部將李光弼以治軍嚴整著稱，主持太原城防；安祿山攻破潼關、長安失守之後，行在靈武的肅宗收攏散兵，詔令各道兵馬歸節度使節制，並借迴紥與僕固部騎兵之援共救河東。叛軍方面以范陽為根本，控弦之士多為幽州、雲中以及蕃胡健兒，配以河北新降州縣的丁夫，攻城則依賴撞車、雲梯、穴地等器械，分批投入兵力試探城防。太原一城，繫著河東兵源的存亡，也卡在叛軍西進洛陽、長安的通道上，故雙方皆不留手。史家多以此役為安史之亂中最完整的守城戰例之一。
countriesEn: The Battle of Taiyuan was a recurring struggle for the great Hedong stronghold of Taiyuan fought between the An-Shi rebel regime and the Tang court from the end of 755 into the year 757. One side was the rebel group led by An Lushan, his son An Qingxu, and the generals Shi Siming and Cui Qianyou; the other was the Tang army of the Hedong and Shuofang circuits, together with steppe horsemen who submitted to the dynasty during the turmoil. On the Tang side the military administration of Hedong rested with the jiedushi Guo Ziyi, while his subordinate Li Guangbi, famous for the strictness and skill of his command, directed the defense of the city. After An Lushan broke through Tong Pass and Chang'an fell, the restored emperor Suzong at Lingwu gathered the scattered troops, ordered the soldiers of every circuit to report to their jiedushi, and borrowed the help of Uighur and Pugu cavalry to relieve Hedong. The rebels drew their strength on Fanyang: their bowmen were largely Hu and Jiankun veterans of Youzhou and Yunzhong, with the dings of the newly subjugated prefectures of Hebei to draw on, and to take a city they relied on battering rams, scaling ladders, sapping and similar machines, feeding their assault in successive waves to test the defenses. Taiyuan was a city on which the manning of Hedong depended, and at the same time the gate through which the rebels would march on Luoyang and Chang'an, so neither side held back. Historians generally treat this battle as one of the most complete surviving examples of siege defense within the An-Shi rebellion.
people: 安祿山是本役的起點，也是最大的變數。他兼領范陽、平盧、河東三鎮節度使，握有北方精兵，卻久蓄吞併河北之志；天寶十四載（755）十二月，他自范陽起兵，率大軍西進，節節攻破河北州縣，兵鋒直指洛陽與河中。太原太守顏杲卿起兵響應朝廷，閉城拒賊而被俘，父子先後殉國，顏氏一門之忠烈自此傳於史冊。安祿山在太原城下受挫折兵，退保范陽，至德元載（756）正月背生惡瘡而死，軍權由其子安慶緒與猛將史思明接掌。史思明驍勇善騎，屢破唐軍，卻久攻太原不下，至德二載（757）唐軍反攻兩京時，他終於放棄河東，退回范陽。主持城防的是李光弼。他出身北方將門，父李楷亦為河東守將，治軍嚴整，能把團練、義勇雜卒整飭成可以倚重的守軍；史家相傳有「用之則行、棄之則散」之語，批評當時河北募兵未經訓練、聚散隨人，李光弼的整軍正是針對此病。郭子儀則總攬河東軍政，居中調度，穩住關中的門戶。僕固懷恩率本部及迴紥騎兵馳援，解了太原之圍，成為平叛戰局轉折的關鍵人物。玄宗西幸、肅宗靈武即位所形成的兩重朝廷，也在此役之中確定了平叛的權力中心。
peopleEn: An Lushan was both the origin of this campaign and its greatest variable. He held the three commands of Fanyang, Pinglu and Hedong, and with them the best troops in the north, yet for long he had harbored the intention of swallowing Hebei; in the twelfth month of 755 he rose at Fanyang and marched west with the main body of his army, breaking the prefectures of Hebei one after another and driving at Luoyang and Hezhong. Yan Gaoqing, governor of Taiyuan, raised troops to answer the court, shut the city against the rebels and was taken prisoner; father and son were martyred in turn, and the loyalty of the Yan clan was handed down to later Tang historiography. After being checked and blooded beneath the walls of Taiyuan, An Lushan fell back on Fanyang and died of a malignant sore on his back in the first month of 756, leaving the command to his son An Qingxu and to the ferocious general Shi Siming. Shi Siming was a superb horseman who beat Tang forces again and again, yet he could not take Taiyuan; in 757, when the Tang counter-offensive drove him from Luoyang, he finally gave up Hedong and withdrew to Fanyang. The defense of the city was directed by Li Guangbi, who came of a northern line of commanders, his father Li Kai having been a garrison commander in Hedong himself. Li drilled the miscellaneous tuanlian and volunteer levy into troops that could be relied upon, and historians hand down a saying that such men serve well only while commanded and scatter once dismissed, a stricture on the undisciplinated recruited soldiers of Hebei that his reorganization was aimed squarely at. Guo Ziyi directed the wider military administration of Hedong and held the balance that kept the gateway of Guanzhong open. Pugu Huai'en brought the cavalry of his own Pugu clan and of the Uighurs to the relief of the city, and the lifting of that siege was the turning point of the whole campaign. The double court created by Xuanzong's flight west and Suzong's accession at Lingwu also fixed, in the course of this battle, where the legitimate authority of the war against the rebels would lie.
kits: 本卡兵器秦連弩，是把拉力儲存於弩機、一踩一發的重複射擊器械，源於戰國秦弩的機括傳統；楚漢之際的連弩更臻成熟，後世稱為「諸葛弩」。入唐之後，連弩的具體形制在文獻中已不易確考，但唐軍城防的火力骨架仍以弩為主：守軍以各式弩機列於城垛、敵樓與女牆，單兵用蹶張弩與角弓弩，重型者即床子弩，架在木牀或望山車上，擊發迅速，最適合對付成群結隊的攻城步兵。與弩並列的，還有弓箭、唐橫刀（儀刀）、陌刀、步槊，以及披甲與明光鎧一類的防護；弩手按射手、裝矢手與護手分列，箭桿以竹為之，至於弓弩的具體尺寸與每城配備數量，史無明文可考。攻城一方則備有撞車、雲梯、木馬與穴地之具，並以飛石機削擊牆頭。守方除城樓女牆之外，又有拒馬、鹿角與壕溝可資利用。補給方面，糧車、汲水與運糧隊維持城內所需，馬匹則集中在叛軍的騎兵與載運上。因此在本役之中，弩的主要作用不在野戰，而在把攻城者壓在牆外，替守軍爭取每一次反擊與整頓的時間。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card, the Qin repeating crossbow, is a device that stores the draw in the lock and releases a bolt with a single step of the foot, and it descends from the trigger mechanism of the Qin crossbow of the Warring States; the repeating crossbow of the Chu-Han period was more mature still, and later generations called it the Zhuge crossbow. After it entered the Tang, the exact form of the repeating crossbow is no longer easy to establish from the surviving literature, yet the firepower skeleton of Tang city defense still rested on the crossbow: the garrison mounted crossbows of various types on the wall walks, the guard towers and the parapets, the individual soldier using the drawn crossbow and the horn bow, while the heavy types were the bed crossbows, set on a wooden bed or on the wheeled elevating frame, quick to fire and ideally suited to masses of assaulting infantry. Alongside the crossbow the defenders had bows and arrows, the Tang sword known as the ceremonial dao, the long Tang saber, the spear, and such protection as leather and lacquered armor; the crossbowmen were organized into shooters, loaders and guards, with bamboo shafts to the bolts, while the exact dimensions of the bows and crossbows and the number of them per city are not recorded. The besiegers brought battering rams, scaling ladders, movable towers and sapping, and used stone-throwing engines to strip the wall heads. The defenders, besides their towers and parapets, could use cheval-de-frise, sharpened stakes and ditches. On the supply side, grain carts, water drawing and transport columns sustained the city, while the horses belonged mainly to the rebel cavalry and to the baggage trains. The point of all this is that in this battle the crossbow was not a field-of-battle weapon but the means of holding the assaulting columns against the wall, buying time for every counter-stroke and every reorganization of the garrison.
tactics: 守城方採的是「閉外郭、守內城、待其自斃」之策。太原城垣厚峻，叛軍攻城先以飛石與投石機削其女牆，再以雲梯貼城、撞車撞門。守軍的應對集中於數事：其一，把弩手分層配置於城頭、敵樓與女牆之內，交叉覆蓋城根，令白日攀城之敵無處可援；其二，設法破壞攻城器械，據記載唐軍曾於夜中出城焚毀敵方雲梯與撞車，使攻城器具屢得屢失；其三，反守為攻，或穿地道直抵敵營，或出城夜襲，毀其攻具與行列；其四，閉城不與戰，專待敵氣餒，避免在城外白白野戰消耗。叛軍則倚仗兵力優勢實行輪番疊攻，把雲梯、撞車、穴地同時推向城垣的不同地段，使守軍顧此失彼；又以騎兵列陣城外游鬥，試圖引唐軍出城反擊，再於野地殲之。補給上，叛軍糧道綿長、久攻無援，最終因糧盡而退；唐軍則靠河東本地的屯田、鹽利與人力支撐，圍城日久，軍中乏食而不潰。此役所見的守城之法，後來成為唐宋之間城防記述反覆引用的樣本。
tacticsEn: The defense followed the plan of sealing the outer works, holding the inner city and waiting for the enemy to exhaust himself. The walls of Taiyuan were thick and high; the rebels first stripped the parapets with stone-throwing engines, then brought scaling ladders against the wall and rams against the gates. The garrison's answers clustered into four kinds. First, the crossbowmen were posted in layers inside the wall heads, the guard towers and the parapets, so that their fire crossed over the foot of the wall and left the men climbing in daylight without a place to draw support. Second, the attacking machines had to be destroyed; the record has the Tang troops going out at night to burn the enemy's ladders and rams, so that the siege equipment was won and lost again and again. Third, the defense turned into offense: men were sent out through tunnels toward the enemy camp, or sorties were made at night to destroy the engines and disorder the ranks. Fourth, the city simply refused to come out and fight, waiting for the enemy to lose heart rather than squandering the garrison in an open battle. The rebels answered with weight of numbers and successive waves, pressing ladders, rams and sappers against different sections of the wall at the same time so that the defenders could not be everywhere at once; they also posted cavalry outside the walls to skirmish, hoping to lure the Tang out and destroy them in the open. On logistics, the rebel army's line of supply was long and no relief came; it finally withdrew because its grain ran out. The Tang held on by means of the local tuntian, the salt revenue and the labor of Hedong, and though the siege ran long and the garrison went hungry, it did not break. The siege methods seen here later became a standing example quoted again and again in Tang and Song writing on the defense of cities.
data: 有關數字多出於《資治通鑑》《舊唐書》《新唐書》與唐人奏議，彼此轉述多有出入，宜作量級參考。安祿山起兵時，叛軍號稱十五萬，其中相當一部分是幽州、雲中以及蕃胡健兒；唐廷方面，朔方、河東兩軍為精銳所在，全國常備兵雖以數十萬計，卻多屯嶺南、劍南、隴右，河北與關中空虛。至德二載（757）唐軍反攻時，集合兵力約十五萬，會同迴紥騎兵收復長安、洛陽。圍攻太原的時段，約起自755年12月叛軍抵達城下，至756年正月解圍，前後不足兩月，叛軍在城下折損兵馬以萬計，其後退回范陽；唐軍亦乘勝追擊，一度重奪安祿山在河北的根據地。城池方面，太原距洛陽約四百五十公里，距長安約九百公里，距離其實不遠，但河東地勢險固、糧秣自足，唐軍因此得以不必分兵。數字上亦須留意：所謂「斬首萬餘級」「死者數萬」等說法，來自不同史家的轉述，彼此未必相容，檔案殘缺之處居多。
dataEn: The numbers here come mostly from the Zizhi Tongjian, the Old and New Tang histories and Tang memorial literature, and the figures quoted in one source rarely match those in another, so they are best read as orders of magnitude. When An Lushan rose, the rebel host was reckoned at a hundred and fifty thousand, a considerable share of them Hu and Jiankun veterans from Youzhou and Yunzhong. On the Tang side, the armies of Shuofang and Hedong were the picked troops, while the national paper strength, counted in the hundreds of thousands, lay mostly in Lingnan, Jiannan and Longyou, leaving Hebei and Guanzhong hollow. When the Tang counter-offensive came in 757, roughly a hundred and fifty thousand men were assembled, and with the help of Uighur cavalry they retook Chang'an and Luoyang. The siege of Taiyuan ran from about the twelfth month of 755, when the rebels reached the walls, to the first month of 756, when it was relieved - a matter of less than two months - and the rebels lost men in the thousands by the foot of the wall before falling back on Fanyang; the Tang pursued them and for a moment recovered An Lushan's base in Hebei. As to distances, Taiyuan lies roughly four hundred and fifty kilometres from Luoyang and about nine hundred from Chang'an; the road is not long, but Hedong's terrain is strong and its grain sufficient, so the Tang did not have to divide their forces. One caution applies to the figures: statements such as the numbers slain or the numbers dead come from different historians and need not be compatible with each other, and the underlying record is in places badly damaged.
cause: 太原之戰的起因，是安史之亂由河北燃起之後，叛軍與唐廷在河東的第一次決定性碰撞。安祿山兼領范陽、平盧、河東三鎮節度使，掌北方精兵而久有異志；玄宗晚年怠政，河北軍鎮久不更代，府兵之制早已崩壞，募兵多出市井，裝備與戰力都遠不及開元盛世的鼎盛。755年十一月安祿山反於范陽，十二月兵鋒南下，接連攻取河北州縣，直指洛陽；太原所在的河東，緊扼河北通向關中的門戶，叛軍若要西進，必先拔此城。與此同時，太原太守顏杲卿等響應朝廷，閉城拒賊，使叛軍西進的日程為之中斷。朝廷在潼關失守、長安淪陷之後才被迫改弦更張：由一味的城市保衛，轉為依靠河東、朔方兩軍與各道勤王之兵重建北方防線，李光弼整飭河東兵、倚太原城為根本，正是這一轉變的產物。至德二載，叛軍因安祿山之死而內部混亂，唐廷乘機反攻，太原之役遂由一場孤城的防守戰，延伸為爭奪兩京的總攻。
causeEn: The battle came about because the An-Shi rebellion, kindled in Hebei, produced its first decisive collision with the Tang in Hedong. An Lushan held the three commands of Fanyang, Pinglu and Hedong, and with them the finest troops in the north, and for long he had harbored wider designs. Under the late Xuanzong government was slack, the Hebei commands went years without reassignment, the fubing militia system had long since fallen apart, and the recruited soldiers came largely from the towns, with equipment and fighting quality far below the height of the Kaiyuan era. In the eleventh month of 755 An Lushan rose at Fanyang; in the twelfth his army drove south, taking the prefectures of Hebei in turn and pressing toward Luoyang. Hedong, in which Taiyuan stood, gripped the gateway from Hebei into Guanzhong, and the rebels could not march west without first taking the city. At the same time the governor of Taiyuan, Yan Gaoqing, and others answered the court's call, shut the city against the rebels and interrupted the rebel timetable for the western march. Only after Tong Pass fell and Chang'an was lost did the court force itself to change its methods: from a plain defense of cities to a rebuilding of the northern line on the armies of Hedong and Shuofang together with the relief columns of the various circuits, and Li Guangbi's reorganization of the Hedong troops and reliance on the city of Taiyuan were products of that change. In 757 the death of An Lushan threw the rebel regime into confusion, the court seized the moment to counter-attack, and the battle of Taiyuan, begun as the defense of a single city, was drawn into the general offensive for the two capitals.
impact: 此役的直接影響，是河東兵源與北方防線得以保全。唐廷正是以河東、朔方兩軍為骨幹重建北方防線，太原自755年之後再未陷落，直到其後河北藩鎮割據與涿郡之亂才換了主人。安史之亂最終能平，唐軍收復兩京、反攻河北的兵力，主要來自河東、朔方與迴紥騎兵；太原一城不陷，等於護住了重建唐朝的兩根柱子。制度上，此役之後唐廷改以節度使掌軍、募兵為主力，府兵與府庫之制一去不返，兵源與裝備的長期代差成為藩鎮割據的溫床。文化上，顏杲卿、顏真卿父子以及太原陷落前後一批死節的官吏，讓「忠義」成為此後數百年間唐史敘述反覆引用的模範；而李光弼治軍的嚴整，也成為後世評述唐代將領的常見尺規。武器上，太原城頭的弩機與其後的床子弩，反映出唐宋之際冷兵器城防的技術上限：此時火藥武器尚未真正投入戰場，射程、射速與攻城器械的較量，仍然決定一座城池的生死。
impactEn: The direct effect of the battle was that the manning of Hedong and the northern line were preserved. The Tang rebuilt the defense of the north on the armies of Hedong and Shuofang; Taiyuan was never taken again after 755, and did not change hands until the later warlord secession in Hebei and the fighting at Zhuojun. Because the An-Shi rebellion could be brought to an end at all, and because the Tang could retake the two capitals and drive back into Hebei, the credit belongs to the troops of Hedong and Shuofang together with the Uighur cavalry; a Taiyuan that did not fall was the same thing as the two pillars on which the dynasty was rebuilt. In institutional terms, after this campaign the court ran its armies through the jiedushi and relied on recruited soldiers as the main body; the fubing and the treasury system of the state were gone for good, and the long gap between the quality of troops and their equipment became the breeding ground of military governors with their own armies. In the writing of the age, Yan Gaoqing, his son Yan Zhenqing and the officials who died for the dynasty around the fall of Taiyuan made loyalty a model that Tang historiography quoted again and again for centuries, and the severity of Li Guangbi's command became a standard measure by which later writers judged Tang generals. As for arms, the crossbows on the wall heads of Taiyuan and the bed crossbows that followed them show the technical ceiling of cold-weapon siege defense in the Tang-Song transition: gunpowder weapons had not yet truly entered the field, and range, rate of fire and the contest with siege engines still decided whether a city lived or died.
result: 結果是唐軍在太原城下取得一場關鍵的守城勝利，而這場勝利最終導向叛軍的全面退潮。天寶十四載末，叛軍初抵太原城下即受挫，安祿山折兵退回范陽，被迫改走潼關一路；潼關失守、長安淪陷之後，叛軍一度聲勢浩大，但河東與朔方兩軍未散，太原未降，史思明在北方雖屢勝，卻始終無法打通河東、直下關中。至德元載（756）正月安祿山死，安慶緒與史思明內部相爭，唐肅宗在靈武即位、詔令勤王，至德二載（757）調集大軍十五萬反攻，會同迴紥騎兵於九月收復長安、十月進取洛陽，安慶緒北走，史思明放棄河東退保范陽，太原之圍至此完全解除。此役之後，叛軍的攻勢由爭取關中與兩京，轉為困守河北；雖然史思明在758年再度反攻、造成新的波折，唐廷最遲在763年前後平定主要叛亂，餘波延續到875年方告結束。太原則成為叛亂年代裡唯一不曾被攻破的北方大城，它保住了河東的兵、糧與匠戶，也保住了唐廷得以反攻的根據地。史家多以「關中不守而太原不陷」來說明此役的分量，細節雖有諸說並存，其大體走向則相當一致。
resultEn: The result was a decisive Tang success beneath the walls of Taiyuan, and that success in the end led to a general ebb of the rebel tide. When the rebels first reached the city at the end of 755 they were checked at once; An Lushan lost men, withdrew to Fanyang and was compelled to try the road through Tong Pass instead. After Tong Pass fell and Chang'an was lost the rebels were for a time at their most imposing, but the armies of Hedong and Shuofang had not dissolved and Taiyuan had not surrendered, and though Shi Siming won again and again in the north he could never open the way through Hedong down into Guanzhong. In the first month of 756 An Lushan died and An Qingxu and Shi Siming quarreled over the succession; Suzong was enthroned at Lingwu and called on the circuits for men, and in 757 a host of some hundred and fifty thousand was assembled for the counter-offensive, retaking Chang'an in the ninth month and advancing into Luoyang in the tenth with the help of the Uighur cavalry. An Qingxu fled north, Shi Siming gave up Hedong and fell back on Fanyang, and the siege of Taiyuan was completely lifted. After this the rebel offensive, which had aimed at Guanzhong and the two capitals, turned into a defense of Hebei; although Shi Siming counter-attacked again in 758 and caused fresh trouble, the main rebellion was finally put down by about 763 and its embers did not die out until 875. Taiyuan became the one great northern city of the rebellious years that was never taken; it preserved the soldiers, the grain and the craftsmen of Hedong, and with them the base from which the Tang could counter-attack. Historians commonly weigh the campaign in the phrase that Guanzhong fell while Taiyuan did not, and although the details remain disputed, the broad shape of the outcome is remarkably consistent.
